title: Saw II
full_review:
In G.K. Chesterton's 1912 comic short novel "Manalive," his protagonist, Innocent Smith, threatens to kill a man to instill in him a deeper appreciation of life. A much grislier version of that tactic is adopted by the homicidal mastermind at the center of "Saw II" (Lions Gate), the repellent follow-up to 2004's horror hit.

Unlike Chesterton's story, the film's opening (and perhaps sickest) scene gleefully assures viewers, "Oh, yes, there will be blood!" -- a promise it makes good on.

Donnie Wahlberg stars here as Eric Matthews, a hard-nosed police detective whose estranged teenage son (Erik Knudsen) -- along with eight other victims -- becomes the newest pawn in a sadistic game of life and death elaborately engineered by the serial killer nicknamed "Jigsaw" (Tobin Bell).

Directed by Darren Lynn Bousman, the sequel follows the original's lead in conceiving ever more twisted ways to kill and maim while packaging torturous cruelty as shock entertainment.

The film contains pervasive bloody violence and gore, including bodily mutilation and a scene of someone burned alive, brief drug content, much rough and crude language and profanity. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted.
